marks.gloss_en: לא, לעולם אימא לך... the baraita may speak of a house known to be unchecked, where the sayers are believed because bedika is rabbinic (mideoraita bittul suffices) -- so it decides nothing about the presumption
the baraita's case: a house we KNOW was not checked by its owner, and these say 'we checked it' -- so it shows nothing about the presumption
תא שמע דאמר אביי: a person is glad to fulfill the mitzva even at his own cost -- so the unchecked house is no mistaken transaction
Abaye: even where people pay a wage to have the search done, a person is glad to fulfill a mitzva with his money
the tanna's premise on the presumption-reading: all are chaverim with regard to bedika, as with the chaver who died
one rented a house as checked and found it unchecked: is the deal a mistaken transaction?
R' Meir: chametz may be eaten through the entire fifth hour
the two verses are reconciled by including the 14th for biur
